question: What are Walmart's lease obligations (operating and finance) and how big are they relative to total assets?

answer.summary: Walmart's operating lease liability as of January 31, 2024 was $14.43B [F00788], comprising $1.49B current [F00131] and $12.94B noncurrent [F00139]. Finance lease liability was $6.43B [F00789], comprising $725.00M current [F00133] and $5.71B noncurrent [F00141]. Total assets were $252.40B [F00119]. The corresponding right-of-use assets were $13.67B for operating leases [F00111] (5.4% of total assets) and $5.86B for finance leases [F00113] (2.3% of total assets). The evidence does not provide a pre-computed ratio of total lease liabilities to total assets, so the combined lease obligation figure is not stated. Operating lease liability of $14.43B [F00788] exceeds finance lease liability of $6.43B [F00789].
drivers: PropertyPlantAndEquipmentNet was the largest contributor to the change in total assets: $110.81B = 43.9% of total [F00109], change $10.05B (+10.0%), a swing of $10.05B against a NET total change of only $9.20B (other components offset it; no percentage share is meaningful) <- LARGEST CONTRIBUTOR TO THE CHANGE [F00109].

Walmart US was the largest contributor to the change in total assets by segment: $137.78B = 54.6% of total [F00966], change $7.12B (+5.5%), 77% of the total change <- LARGEST CONTRIBUTOR TO THE CHANGE [F00966].

Finance lease obligations grew +17.9% YoY noncurrent ($4.84B -> $5.71B) [F00141] and +27.9% YoY current ($567.00M -> $725.00M) [F00133], far outpacing operating leases which were essentially flat (+0.9% noncurrent [F00139], +1.0% current [F00131]).
Operating lease right-of-use assets grew +0.9% YoY to $13.67B [F00111], while finance lease right-of-use assets grew +19.0% YoY to $5.86B [F00113].
risks_and_red_flags: Finance lease obligations are growing at ~19% YoY (noncurrent +17.9% [F00141], current +27.9% [F00133]), far outpacing operating leases which were essentially flat (+0.9% [F00139], +1.0% [F00131]), which may signal increasing capital-intensive leasing commitments and higher fixed obligations.

The $34.3B of unrecorded purchase obligations [T00528], of which $14.6B is due within one year, is a separate commitment that should not be conflated with lease obligations but adds to Walmart's overall off-balance-sheet-like commitments.
Only FY2024 total lease liability figures are provided in the evidence; prior-year totals must be derived from the sum of current and noncurrent components [F00131][F00139][F00133][F00141].
data_quality_notes: Only FY2024 total values for OperatingLeaseLiability ($14.43B [F00788]) and FinanceLeaseLiability ($6.43B [F00789]) are provided; FY2023 totals are derived from the sum of current and noncurrent components.
2 duplicate facts with conflicting values were set aside during parsing (the primary-statement value was kept).
The ratio of lease obligations to total assets is not pre-computed in the evidence; only the right-of-use asset percentages of total assets are given (operating 5.4% [F00111], finance 2.3% [F00113]).

outlook.actuals_view: Lease obligations are stable for operating leases but growing for finance leases; no indication of deleveraging in the lease portfolio.
outlook.forward_looking_guidance: Not in the retrieved evidence - no management guidance on lease obligations was provided.

follow_up_checks: Obtain the lease maturity schedule from the notes to financial statements to see future minimum lease payments by year for both operating and finance leases.
Verify whether the finance lease growth relates to specific acquisitions, distribution center build-outs, or real estate transactions.
Confirm the composition of the $34.3B unrecorded purchase obligations [T00528] to ensure no overlap with lease commitments.
